newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says rules on preferred shares unfair.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says rules on preferred shares unfair.

text.p: South Korean regulations requiring listed companies to guarantee cash dividends of at least nine percent for newly issued preferred shares are unfair, the Fair Trade Commission said Monday.
A commission statement said the watchdog agency had decided to ask the Korea Listed Companies Association to delete related rules from its securities regulations.
The association stipulated the rules last October to attract investor interest in preferred shares, which had dividends one percent higher than those on common shares but no voting rights.
The statement said 271 listed companies had guaranteed the minimum dividends for new preferred shares as of March 26.
Four companies offered more than 10 percent dividends for their preferred stocks.
